blocks: Legal foundations, history, philosophy and research
Both introduce legal fields and the operation of law; UCR is comparative and interdisciplinary rather than an LLB foundation sequence.
Natural law, natural rights, legal positivism and universality critiques provide a substantial partial legal-philosophy relationship, centred on human rights rather than all global jurisprudence.
No scheduled UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg's second programme-specific global-law introduction.
UCR distributes perspectives on law across law, politics, sociology and philosophy rather than one dedicated course.
UCR Ethics does not reproduce advanced philosophy of global law.
UCR offers an optional independent research element, but the scheduled programme does not require Tilburg's 12-ECTS legal thesis.
Public, international, European and criminal law
Both examine criminal liability and justice; UCR is comparative and less doctrinally extensive.
Both cover sources, subjects and major fields of public international law.
Both study constitutional limits on public authority; UCR compares multiple systems.
Both address EU institutions, sources, rights, market rules and enforcement.
UCR international law and history courses do not reproduce a dedicated history of international law.
UCR covers cross-border public and commercial questions but has no dedicated conflict-of-laws course.
Private law, commerce, business and regulation
Both address obligations and private-law relationships; UCR offers one broad principles course.
Both address commercial transactions and disputes; UCR has an explicitly transnational scope.
Microeconomic choice, markets, costs and strategic interaction provide partial economic foundations for the business/legal-market questions. No mergers-and-acquisitions specialism is claimed.
UCR private and criminal law discuss liability, but no scheduled course directly reproduces Tilburg's dedicated Tort Law course.
UCR has no second advanced obligations-and-contract law course.
Sustainability, environmental governance and structured choice
Tilburg's 30-ECTS mobility window remains a structured external choice; UCR alternatives instead show three fixed interdisciplinary curricula.
Regional social/gender histories provide context, not a history of legal institutions and traditions.
Empirical business/social methods do not establish the programme-specific comparative/doctrinal legal-method component.
Comparative politics is institutional context; administrative-law content occurs within constitutional law, already assigned to the stronger constitutional relationship.
General sociology is not a criminology course. Criminal-law study is already assigned to its primary criminal-law counterpart.
AI business/regulation provides context, not primary legal analysis of ICT and biotechnology.
Banking/finance is not property and insolvency doctrine. Broad private law includes property but is assigned to its stronger contract relationship.
International business/governance is not a corporate-law subject course.

notes.text: UCR offers a substantial interdisciplinary law curriculum but not Tilburg's 180-ECTS LLB, specialist legal-skills sequence, required legal thesis or Dutch qualifying-law route. These pathways should not be read as qualifying law degrees.

audience.programmeDescription: Global Law at Tilburg University studies legal problems across jurisdictions through comparative, public, private and international law. Legal history, philosophy, research and communication support a broad legal foundation and a required bachelor thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options combine substantive comparative and international legal study with political and social contexts, commercial fields, or environmental governance. They retain gaps in Tilburg’s sustained doctrinal and legal-skills sequence and required legal thesis. Shared rows show partial subject relationships rather than course equivalence or professional qualification.

curriculum.routeLabel: English-language bachelor; standard core with Commercial Law
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC include 30 EC of approved mobility/minor choice and a required 12-EC thesis. Communication skills and GROW include zero-credit activities. Choosing the Dutch Law minor changes the final-year core and is a separate pathway from the one shown.
